_README: Brain-picked platform announcements rendered by https://dchub.cloud/whats-new#platform.
APPROVAL = MERGE. The brain opens a PR that adds or edits an entry here; merging that PR
is the owner's approval. There is no write endpoint, no admin toggle and no cron that
mutates this file. An entry is INVISIBLE unless status is exactly "published" — a draft,
a typo'd status or a missing status is withheld (routes/platform_updates.py::_is_published).
NO FIGURES IN PROSE. The first cards here replaced hardcoded HTML that went stale in public:
it said '36 grids' while the scoreboard ranked 46, and '73 tools' / 'tool #73' while the
live catalog was at 81. So `title` and `body` may not contain a figure — the loader
rejects one (::_looks_like_bare_figure). To show a number, declare a metric TOKEN; the
client binds the value live from /api/v1/canon/phrases at render time. A number that is
never stored can never go stale.
Metric tokens with a live source: tools · facilities · markets · deals · countries.
Any other token is served as UNMEASURED (value null + a reason) and renders no number.
Never invent a token to smuggle a literal back in.
Fields: id (stable, unique) · status · announced (YYYY-MM-DD) · tag · title · body ·
Order in this array is the render order — newest first.

updates.title: Capabilities, read live from the running server
updates.body: Every MCP capability on one page, read from the running server on every load — newest first, with the authoritative upstream sources named, provenance on every response and explicit unknowns instead of confident blanks. The catalog cannot describe a capability the server does not serve.

updates.title: Try the live data in the browser, no signup
updates.body: A playground for the live layers: search the facility inventory, rank power markets by the index, pull the biggest movers and the latest industry news — straight from the browser, no account. When the answers earn it, connect your own AI to the same endpoint you just tried.

updates.title: What the AI models say, verbatim
updates.body: We asked the leading models to rank the data-center intelligence field against the incumbents they already know, and published their verdicts word for word — dated, with the prompts. Read what the agents' own models concluded before an agent ever calls a tool here.

updates.title: A live brief for every scored market
updates.body: Every market the index scores now carries its own daily brief — power verdict, grid context, pipeline, deals, tenants and news for that metro, rebuilt from the live layers on every read. The sections an analyst would assemble, generated from the data instead of about it.

updates.title: Per-hyperscaler pipeline briefs
updates.body: One brief per hyperscaler: announced megawatts, capex, power agreements, acquisitions, ISO exposure and water context, assembled from the same deal and infrastructure layers the MCP tools query — so an agent and its human read the same pipeline.

updates.title: The analyst desk, running daily
updates.body: Live, cited analysis of the infrastructure behind AI: power-market rankings, grid headroom and time-to-power, deal flow and tenant briefs — written from the live layers, refreshed on cadence, every figure carrying its source.

updates.title: Price a site three ways
updates.body: Site valuation compares grid power, behind-the-meter gas and gas-to-grid into a net-present-value view, layered with the power verdict and site-readiness premiums, beside comparable sales. Subscriber tooling, and the paywall states what it withholds.

updates.title: Connect DC Hub to your AI platform, step by step
updates.body: One endpoint, every agent: a walkthrough for adding DC Hub as a custom MCP connector on ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Perplexity, Gemini Enterprise, Le Chat and Grok — with the free tier's scope stated up front. The setup page an agent can hand its human.

updates.title: Where DC Hub stands, measured in public
updates.body: The standing page tracks the registries that list the MCP server, the platforms actively connected, and the search rankings behind the claims — each figure bound at render from the live sources, with the measurement dated. The receipts behind the data layer agents already use.

updates.title: The product surface, rendered from the approved feed
updates.body: Every shipped capability on one page, rendered from the same PR-approved feed that powers these cards — each card names its basis and binds its figures at render time, so the product page cannot claim what the platform does not serve.

updates.title: Tell us what's broken, or missing
updates.body: A public intake for bugs, feature requests, wrong figures and broken links. The brain triages every submission: trivial fixes ship same-day, judgment calls queue for review — and the page shows recent feedback beside what already got fixed because of it.

updates.title: The Grid Transition Radar: a daily briefing, re-voiced for its reader
updates.body: A distinct publication on one live data core: each day's edition reads the grid's energy transition — headroom, retirements, prices, interconnection movement — and renders it in the voice of a different audience on rotation: capital, site selection, agents and press. It is built from the same live layers the MCP tools query, cited the same way, and the current edition is free to preview. Agents get their own machine-readable edition feed.

updates.title: Land & Power beyond the map: Table, Chart and News views
updates.body: The Land & Power map now carries a four-way view switcher. Table renders every loaded layer as a sortable table with CSV export and names the layers it covers; Chart plots loaded features per layer for the current viewport, where a layer toggled off reads as off, never as zero; News puts live infrastructure coverage beside the map, and a failed fetch states its reason instead of posing as an empty list. Honest-empty over pretty-blank, in every view.

updates.title: Research every tracked data center in one database
updates.body: The full facility inventory behind the API is now browsable by humans: filter by market, ISO, operator, capacity and status, sort and map the results, export what you need, and open a complete profile for any site. It is the same de-duplicated inventory the MCP tools answer from — what an agent cites and what a human reads now share one source.

updates.title: The DCPI method is now machine-readable
updates.body: Every DCPI indicator weight, every cap, every verdict band and the full revision history are now served as JSON at /api/v1/dcpi/methodology, emitted from the same constants the scorer imports — so the published method and the live index cannot drift into describing different formulas. The known limitations ship in the same payload, including an input that is never populated and therefore contributes a structural zero to every constraint score.

updates.title: Cross-layer site discovery produces candidates, not rankings
updates.body: GET /api/v1/sites/cross-layer builds a candidate set out of the physical layers themselves — the substation layer is the search space, with fiber coverage, carrier presence, DCPI market context and optional floodplain evidence attached to each anchor — instead of re-ranking a shortlist the caller already had. It also declares what it refuses to answer: constraint_coverage names measured MW headroom as absent from every layer, with the reason, so an agent can see the hole instead of inferring a number nobody measured.

updates.title: The grid scoreboard separates zones ranked from independent feeds
updates.body: get_grid_scoreboard now returns the ranked-zone count and the count of independent upstream feeds as two separate named fields, each with its basis, because one combined figure read as far more independent sourcing than exists — most ranked zones arrive through a single ENTSO-E feed. Neither figure is stored on this card: both move between calls, and DC Hub publishes no keyless grid-zone count to bind against, so what is published here is the split itself.

updates.title: Japan, South Korea & Brazil join the live scoreboard
updates.body: get_grid_scoreboard (keyless, free-tier) now ranks Japan (OCCTO), South Korea (KPX) and Brazil SIN (ONS) beside the US ISOs, EU bidding zones, Great Britain and Taiwan — national grids scored on one real-time renewable-share scale that now spans five continents. Compare grids for LatAm and APAC siting the same way you compare US ISOs; Australia and Singapore are live-partial.

updates.title: Spot interconnection headroom before it opens
updates.body: get_retirement_headroom returns filed US generator retirements (EIA-860M) — coal and gas plants with capacity, retirement date and the nearest substations — so an agent can find where grid interconnection headroom is about to free up as plants retire.

updates.title: Provenance Envelope v1 on facility search
updates.body: search_facilities returns a per-record de-duplication tier — a distinct facility versus one of its source records — plus source, a CC-BY-4.0 license and a citation-URL template. The counts behind it are published live at /api/v1/stats/canonical as facilities_distinct and facilities_records.

updates.title: Your agent remembers your shortlist
updates.body: save_site builds a durable list of candidate sites; next session get_changes returns per-site deltas — verdict flips, DCPI score moves, new nearby facilities — not just global market movers.

updates.title: A machine-readable error contract
updates.body: Every error now carries error_version:1 — a severity class and a deterministic recovery hint, plus a server-computed suggested_params so your agent auto-corrects a bad parameter and re-runs without dropping context.

updates.title: cluster_sites_by_latency joins the catalog
updates.body: Clusters candidate sites by fibre round-trip latency, pruning physically-impossible low-latency pairs against SMF-28 fibre floors before any routing. Live over MCP and at /api/v1/fiber/cluster-latency.
